@@32608592 <p> ( Bonn , 26 February 2021 ) -- UN Climate Change today published the Initial NDC Synthesis Report , showing nations must redouble efforts and submit stronger , more ambitious national climate action plans in 2021 if they 're to achieve the Paris Agreement goal of limiting global temperature rise by 2 ? C -- ideally 1.5 ? C -- by the end of the century . <p> " This report shows that current levels of climate ambition are very far from putting us on a pathway that will meet our Paris Agreement goals , " said Patricia Espinosa , Executive Secretary of UN Climate Change . " While we acknowledge the recent political shift in momentum towards stronger climate action throughout the world , decisions to accelerate and broaden climate action everywhere must be taken now . This underlines why COP 26 must be the moment when we get on track towards a green , clean , healthy and prosperous world . " <p> The report was requested by Parties to the Paris Agreement to measure the progress of national climate action plans -- known as NDCs -- @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ up to 31 December 2020 , it shows 75 Parties have communicated a new or updated NDC , representing approximately 30 per cent of global greenhouse gas emissions . <p> The report shows that while the majority of nations represented increased their individual levels of ambition to reduce emissions , their combined impact puts them on a path to achieve only a 1 per cent reduction by 2030 compared to 2010 levels . The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change , by contrast , has indicated that emission reduction ranges to meet the 1.5 ? C temperature goal should be around 45 per cent lower . <p> Espinosa clarified that the Synthesis Report is a " snapshot , not a full picture " of the NDCs as COVID-19 posed significant challenges for many nations with respect to completing their submissions in 2020 . She indicated that a second report will be released prior to COP26 and called on all countries -- specifically major emitters that have not yet done so -- to make their submissions as soon as possible , so that their information can be included in the updated report @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ challenges posed by COVID-19 in 2020 , honoured their commitments under the Paris Agreement and submitted their NDCs by the deadline , " said Ms. Espinosa , " but it 's time for all remaining Parties to step up , fulfil what they promised to do under the Paris Agreement and submit their NDCs as soon as possible . If this task was urgent before , it 's crucial now . " <p> She noted that 2021 gives the world an unprecedented opportunity to make significant progress on climate change and urged all nations to build forward from COVID-19 with more sustainable and climate-resilient economies . " This is a rare moment that can not be lost , " Espinosa said . " As we rebuild , we can not revert to the old normal . The NDCs must reflect this reality and major emitters , especially G20 nations , must lead the way . " <p> Incoming COP26 President Alok Sharma said : " This report should serve as an urgent Call to Action and I am asking all countries , particularly major emitters , to submit ambitious 2030 @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ that the window for action to safeguard our planet is closing fast " , he added . <p> COP25 President Carolina Schmidt noted that this NDC Synthesis Report " clearly indicated that significant work must be done , in particular by major emitters . @@32611913 <p> Who is legally responsible for protecting our ice caps ? Could a Polar approach to climate change strengthen political and legal responses to climate change and other human activities in both the Arctic and Antarctic regions ? University of Canterbury ... <p> Who is legally responsible for protecting our ice caps ? Could a Polar approach to climate change strengthen political and legal responses to climate change and other human activities in both the Arctic and Antarctic regions ? <p> University of Canterbury ( UC ) Law Professor Karen Scott and Professor David VanderZwaag ( Dalhousie University , Canada ) , editors of the Polar Law Research Handbook explore these and other questions of law and policy relating to the Antarctic and Arctic in their new book , published in December 2020 . <p> " We 're exploring whether we can readily and clearly identify a set of rules and principles that apply across the Polar regions , acknowledging , however , that the Arctic and Antarctic regions are different in many ways , " Professor Scott says . <p> " There are Indigenous Peoples in the Arctic , @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ geo-political situation is quite different . The Arctic is largely under the sovereignty of a number of states whereas the Antarctic is managed as an international space under the Antarctic Treaty System . " <p> " In editing the Polar Law Research Handbook we were able to identify five broad principles that could underpin an emerging Polar Law . These include a strong cooperative and internationalised approach to regional governance , peaceful purposes , freedom and cooperation in scientific research , strong environmental protection and an emerging precautionary approach to climate change . And there is plenty of opportunity for the two regions to learn from each other and exchange best practise in order to improve how activities are managed at the Poles , " she says . <p> One possible benefit of identifying Polar Law ( beyond law which applies to the Poles ) is that it enhances the authority of the law , both within the regions themselves but also within other organisations such as the United Nations ( UN ) and the climate change regime . <p> Professor Scott says both regions have been wary of addressing @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Arctic Council until recently . <p> " States argue that it 's not activities taking place in the Polar Regions that are causing climate change and there is a more appropriate forum to address climate change : the UN climate change regime . But in both Polar regimes , states have committed to protect the environment and it could be argued that in order to meet those commitments at the Poles states must take action to address climate change within their metropolitan state . This argument gets stronger as both regimes begin to take more action on climate change regionally , but unsurprisingly , this argument has not yet been accepted by key Polar states , including New Zealand ! " <p> The Edward Elgar Research Handbook on Polar Law Research brings together 35 leading international researchers exploring the Polar Law that applies to territory , peoples and activities in the Arctic and Antarctic regions .

Perhaps the best way @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ government ' is to recognise governance as a noun and government as a verb . <p> Governance is the name given to the entire suite of neoliberal decision-making processes : the whole professional , credentialed , expert hierarchy of policy-advisers ; people who consider themselves " best qualified " to " know " what must be done . <p> Government is what those whose duty it is to make decisions actually do . And that is determined not only by their personal judgement , but also by their understanding of what the people who made them decision-makers need and want . <p> Bringing those needs and wants into some sort of rough harmony is what democratic politics is all about . It can not happen without spirited and open debate , and spirited and open debate can not happen unless the people 's elected representatives are free to speak their minds . <p> But this is precisely what neoliberalism fears the most : the intrusion of popular needs and wants into a capitalist system which depends for its proper functioning on human needs and wants manifesting themselves exclusively in the @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ an elected body to over-ride market signals , then the proper functioning of the free-market capitalism must inevitably be deranged . One collection of interests will find itself in a position to dominate another -- to the ultimate disadvantage of all interests . As far as the neoliberals are concerned , democracy and capitalism are incompatible . <p> This explains why words like " dysfunctional " and " irresponsible " get thrown about the moment the political noise rises above the low murmur of dignified agreement . When a councillor stands up and defies the comfortable owners of Victorian villas on behalf of rack-rented citizens in need of large-scale social housing developments . Or , when a veteran of the sixties youth rebellion openly manoeuvres for his city 's largest employer to be kept going -- regardless of all the market signals flashing red . <p> In the ears of the neoliberals , passionate policy debates register as little more than the whooping and chest-beating of Chimpanzees : mindless status displays ; idiotic battles for recognition and dominance . Uncontrolled democracy drowns out the signals of the marketplace , making @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ needed to decode its messages to be heard . <p> That is why , for the past 35 years , neoliberals have been moving as much of the machinery of government as far out of the reach of all these posturing political apes as possible . But it seems that this new Government is getting serious about tackling climate change . Last year , we saw the declaration of a climate change emergency . That measure included a commitment for a carbon-neutral public service , including transitioning the fleet to EVs . <p> An emergency of this type is largely symbolic but politically significant . If the Government does n't take action commensurate to an ' emergency ' , it will give the opposition plenty of fodder . Much of that action needs to take place over the next 10 @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Clean Car Import Standard , and signaled that an incentive for electric vehicles is coming soon . There has been , as expected , some discussion about how fast this standard should be implemented . <p> As I see it , as an advanced economy New Zealand is pretty much alone in not having emissions limits for our vehicles . Further , the standards proposed for 2025 have already been hit in Japan and the European Union . <p> When we look ahead , as the Climate Change Commission report does , if Aotearoa is to achieve a low emissions vehicle fleet by 2050 , all light vehicles entering the country must be low emissions by 2035 . So , if we 're serious about climate change , we simply have to be brave and show some ambition in moving away from fossil fuel-powered cars . The sooner we signal our intent to car manufacturers around the future mix of vehicles we need in New Zealand , the more time they have to respond . It can be done . Just last month Norway achieved 81 per cent EV penetration @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ affordability of EVs , and the potential for New Zealanders to hold onto older petrol cars if prices start to rise as standards kick in . These are legitimate issues that need to be worked through . <p> When considering transport 's role in climate change , we have to remember however that we are not talking about changes to our cars , SUVs and utes alone . We are talking about fundamental changes to how we get around . This means more active and public transport . It means better designed cities and working from home . It also means thinking about alternatives to car ownership , like car sharing . <p> But many people will still own cars , and businesses will continue to rely on vehicles for commerce . A range of policies need to be developed to encourage car owners to make the switch . A start , of course , is having this national conversation . If New Zealanders know the writing is on the wall for petrol cars , then they can factor this into their decision making when choosing their next vehicle . @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ heads up . <p> Businesses will play a role here too . More than half of the new vehicles entering New Zealand are bought by corporates . Therefore , we need to look at how to encourage these owners to switch to EVs . Adjustments to depreciation and FBT may help , as will expectations of businesses to reduce their own carbon footprints . Promised new laws mandating the disclosure of climate risk in financial reporting will shift expectations of business action to new levels . <p> For everyday Kiwis , it 's also about making EV ownership desirable and easy . If people ca n't access charging infrastructure that works , a transition will fail completely . Incentives will likely be necessary in the short-term to kickstart a rapid uptake of EVs . At this stage EVs are still more expensive than equivalent fossil-fueled vehicles . Parity may come reasonably quickly , but the Commission report suggests we do n't have time to wait . <p> Effort must now be directed to developing a suite of policies and necessary incentives and investments to plan this generational shift in how @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ The Climate Change Commission goes well beyond transport , and signals changes in forestry , agriculture , heating , electricity generation and other sectors . It is very much worth paying attention to .
